questions.question: Gugga Naumi is mainly celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Gugga Naumi is a snake-worship festival celebrated primarily in Haryana and parts of Punjab and Rajasthan.
  • The festival is dedicated to Gugga Ji (Guga Pir), a folk deity believed to protect against snake bites.
  • It is observed on the ninth day (Naumi) of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada.
  • Note: A procession is usually taken out featuring a 'Chhari' (a long decorated pole) to the accompaniment of Deru drums.

questions.question: ‘Bathukammas’ is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Bathukamma is a vibrant floral festival celebrated by the women of Telangana.
  • The name literally means 'Mother Goddess come Alive' and is celebrated during the latter half of the monsoon, before the onset of winter.
  • Women build beautiful stacks of local seasonal flowers in concentric layers, forming a conical shape to honor Goddess Gauri.
  • Additional Info: It falls during the Navratri festival and ends on Durgashtami.

questions.question: Pongal is a four-day-long harvest festival, which is celebrated at the harvest of crops like sugarcane and __________.
questions.solution:
Pongal is a major harvest festival where Rice and sugarcane are the primary crops celebrated.
  • The word 'Pongal' in Tamil means 'to boil over' or 'spill over,' symbolizing abundance and prosperity.
  • The traditional dish, also called Pongal, is made from the newly harvested Rice, boiled with milk and jaggery.
  • Note: It is a four-day festival consisting of Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal, and Kaanum Pongal.

questions.question: From which state, the performing art 'Ottamthullal' belongs?
questions.solution:
Ottamthullal is a unique performing art and dance-drama form from Kerala.
  • It was introduced in the 18th century by the legendary poet Kunchan Nambiar.
  • It is known for its humor, social satire, and the simplicity of its language, unlike the more formal Kathakali.
  • Feature: The performer acts, sings, and dances simultaneously while wearing distinctive green makeup and a colorful headgear.

questions.question: Independence Day is celebrated at the national level at ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­__________ in Delhi.
questions.solution:
India's Independence Day (15th August) is celebrated at the national level at the Red Fort in Delhi.
  • The Prime Minister of India hoists the Tricolor flag and delivers a speech from the ramparts of this historic monument.
  • The Red Fort was the main residence of the Mughal Emperors and remains a symbol of India's sovereignty.
  • Note: India Gate is more closely associated with the Republic Day parade.

questions.question: ‘Matho Nagrang’ is associated with which of the following states/UTs?
questions.solution:
Matho Nagrang is a significant monastic festival celebrated in the Ladakh Union Territory.
  • It takes place at the Matho Monastery, the only monastery in Ladakh belonging to the Sakya school of Tibetan Buddhism.
  • The highlight of the festival is the appearance of two oracles who perform sacred mask dances (Cham).
  • Fact: The oracles are believed to predict the future of the community for the coming year.

questions.question: “Ambubachi Mela” is associated with which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The Ambubachi Mela is a major annual festival held at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam.
  • It celebrates the yearly menstruation course of the Goddess Kamakhya.
  • It is often referred to as the 'Mahakumbh of the East' as it attracts thousands of tantric babas and devotees from all over India.
  • Note: The temple remains closed for three days during this period and reopens on the fourth day with great festivities.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the festival Vishu celebrated?
questions.solution:
Vishu is the Hindu festival marking the Malayalam New Year in Kerala.
  • The most important ritual is 'Vishukkani', where people view an arrangement of auspicious items (like gold, fruits, and flowers) first thing in the morning.
  • Other traditions include Vishu Kaineettam (giving money to younger members) and a grand feast called Vishu Sadya.
  • Timing: It usually falls in the middle of April, coinciding with the spring equinox.

questions.question: _________ is the main festival of Karnataka, which marks the Kannada new year.
questions.solution:
Ugadi is the festival that marks the beginning of the New Year according to the Hindu lunar calendar in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
  • The name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Yuga' (age) and 'Adi' (beginning).
  • A special dish called Bevu-Bella (made of Neem and Jaggery) is consumed to symbolize that life is a mixture of bitterness and sweetness.
  • Note: In Maharashtra, this same New Year is celebrated as Gudi Padwa.

questions.question: ‘Amongmong Festival’ is associated with which of the following states/UTs?
questions.solution:
The Amongmong Festival is an important harvest festival celebrated by the Sangtam tribe of Nagaland.
  • The festival lasts for six days and is dedicated to worshiping the deity of the house for a good harvest and prosperity.
  • It involves traditional dances, folk songs, and the sharing of meat and local brews among the community.

questions.question: How many National Festivals does India celebrate?
questions.solution:
India officially celebrates Three National Festivals.
  • Republic Day: Celebrated on January 26th to mark the adoption of the Constitution.
  • Independence Day: Celebrated on August 15th to mark freedom from British rule.
  • Gandhi Jayanti: Celebrated on October 2nd to honor the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi.
  • Note: These are gazetted holidays observed across all states and Union Territories regardless of religion or culture.

questions.question: The Nuakhai festival is mainly seen in which state?
questions.solution:
Nuakhai is an agricultural festival primarily celebrated by the people of Western Odisha.
  • The name 'Nua' means new and 'Khai' means food, signifying the eating of the newly harvested rice.
  • The first grains of the harvest are offered to Goddess Samaleswari in Sambalpur.
  • Additional Info: It is a symbol of brotherhood as families gather together to share the first meal of the season.

questions.question: From which state, 'Pongal' festival belongs?
questions.solution:
Pongal is the primary harvest festival of Tamil Nadu.
  • It is a thanksgiving festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and nature for providing a bountiful harvest.
  • The celebration spans four days, with the second day (Thai Pongal) being the most significant.

questions.question: This festival belongs to Sambalpur (Western Odisha), the new harvest crops are worshipped and people celebrate it by eating the first rice of the harvest together with their family:
questions.solution:
As described, Nuakhai is the festival where the new harvest crops are worshipped in Western Odisha (Sambalpur).
  • The ritual involves 'Nabanna' (offering the new rice) to the presiding deities before the common people consume it.
  • It is celebrated the day after Ganesh Chaturthi.

questions.question: The major festival of ________ 's tribes is kharchi Puja, Garia Puja, Ker Puja, Bizu Festival, Tirtha Mukh Festival, Ashokastami, Ganga Puja, Lampra Puja, Wah festival.
questions.solution:
The state of Tripura is home to various tribes who celebrate festivals like Kharchi Puja and Garia Puja.
  • Kharchi Puja: A week-long festival where 14 deities are worshipped in Old Agartala.
  • Garia Puja: Held on the last day of the month of Chaitra to pray for a good harvest.
  • Note: Bizu is the New Year festival of the Chakma community in Tripura.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is mainly associated with Assam?
questions.solution:
Bihu is the most important set of festivals celebrated in Assam.
  • There are three types: Rongali Bihu (Spring/New Year), Kati Bihu (Autumn), and Magh Bihu (Harvest).
  • It is characterized by the energetic Bihu dance performed by young men and women in traditional attire like the Muga Silk Mekhela Chador.

questions.question: Which one is not the festival of Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The Sunburn Festival is not a festival of Gujarat; it is a world-famous electronic dance music (EDM) festival held in Goa.
  • The other three (Uttarayan, Paragliding, and Kutch Festival) are major tourism events in Gujarat.
  • Uttarayan is the famous International Kite Festival celebrated on January 14th.

questions.question: Which of the following festival is celebrated on 25th December all over the world?
questions.solution:
Christmas is a global festival celebrated on 25th December to commemorate the birth of Jesus Christ.
  • It is observed with religious services, the decoration of Christmas trees, gift-giving, and festive meals.
  • Note: In India, it is a national holiday and is celebrated with great enthusiasm in states like Goa, Kerala, and Meghalaya.

questions.question: Every year the Flamingo festival is celebrated at the Pulicat Lake near the Nellapattu Bird Sanctuary located in __________.
questions.solution:
The Flamingo Festival is held in Andhra Pradesh at Pulicat Lake.
  • The lake is a major stopover for migratory birds, and the festival aims to create awareness about bird conservation.
  • The Nellapattu Bird Sanctuary is one of the largest habitats for Grey Pelicans and other water birds.

questions.question: The spring festival of Holi is celebrated as Yaoshang by the Meitei tribe in the state of ________. lasting about six days.
questions.solution:
Yaoshang is the equivalent of Holi and is the most important festival of the Meitei people in Manipur.
  • It begins on the full moon day of the month of Lamda and lasts for six days.
  • A major feature is the Thabal Chongba, a traditional folk dance where boys and girls join hands and dance in a circle.

questions.question: In which of the following states of India is the festival Baisakhi celebrated?
questions.solution:
Baisakhi (or Vaisakhi) is the premier harvest festival of Punjab.
  • It marks the ripening of the Rabi crop and is celebrated with the high-energy Bhangra and Gidda dances.
  • For Sikhs, it also has deep religious significance as the day Guru Gobind Singh established the Khalsa Panth in 1699.

questions.question: The Ossuary feast festival is celebrated in which of the following states/UTs?
questions.solution:
The Ossuary Feast is a unique ancestral worship festival celebrated in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, specifically by the Nicobarese tribe.
  • It involves the ritual of exhuming the bones of deceased family members to pay them respect and re-burying them.
  • It is a significant communal event involving feasting and traditional canoe races.

questions.question: Baisakhi is the festival of __________.
questions.solution:
While primarily associated with Punjab, Baisakhi is also celebrated with great fervor in Haryana.
  • Farmers express gratitude to God for the bountiful harvest and pray for future prosperity.
  • Mela (fairs) are organized where traditional wrestling and folk music are showcased.

questions.question: Which of following festivals is associated with Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The Modhera Dance Festival (also known as Uttarardh Mahotsav) is a major cultural event held in Gujarat.
  • It takes place at the historic Sun Temple in Modhera, an architectural masterpiece of the Solanki era.
  • The festival showcases classical Indian dance forms against the backdrop of the beautifully lit temple.

questions.question: In which Indian state is the 'International Lusophone Festival’ hosted?
questions.solution:
The International Lusophone Festival is hosted in Goa.
  • The term 'Lusophone' refers to Portuguese-speaking nations.
  • As Goa was a former Portuguese colony, the festival celebrates the historical and cultural links between India and the Lusophone world through music, food, and cinema.
